posts.title: A summary of today's developments
posts.text: Six people have been killed and 16 injured after a gunman opened fire in a busy market square in Kraków on Saturday in what Poland’s defence minister, Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, called an “act of terror” on the people of the city. The suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, opened fire with an automatic weapon from…

Polish prime minister Donald Tusk said the motives behind the attack will be carefully studied as part of the investigation, as he warned against disinformation circulating online. The prime minister also thanked police officers for their swift response, saying they “saved many people’s lives.” Two officers - praised…

The shooting in Poland’s second city of Krakow was an act of “terrorism”, Polish prime minister Donald Tusk said. “Until now in Poland we haven’t had such drastic cases of terrorism,” Tusk told reporters in Krakow, adding: “That’s what we have to call this cruel attack on people’s lives here in Krakow.” Tusk added…

The UK’s PM Andy Burnham wrote on X: “I’m shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting in Kraków today. “My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence. “The United Kingdom stands in solidarity with the people of Poland.”

posts.title: Bodies found inside home of shooter
posts.text: Two women and ⁠one ⁠man, most likely members of the ⁠family of the ⁠Polish gunman ‌who killed ‌six people shooting ‌from a car in the heart of ‌the southern city of Krakow, were found ⁠dead inside of his house, Polish prime minister Donald Tusk ‌said on Saturday. Drone footage appeared to show the dead bodies in the…

posts.title: British citizen killed in shooting
posts.text: A British national was among the six victims killed in the shooting in Krakow, Polish police chief Marek Boron said on Saturday. “There are six fatalities: four women and two men – three Polish women, one British national, and two people who have not yet been identified,” Boron told reporters.

Krakow mayor Łukasz Gibała said the city will be in official mourning until Wednesday, but vowed that Krakow will remain open to visitors despite the tragedy. “The square will belong to us again,” Gibała said in a video posted to X.

Five foreigners were among wounded victims of the shooting in Poland’s city of Krakow, the interior minister Marcin Kierwinski said after a gunman killed six people in the city’s old town. Sixteen people were hospitalised following the shooting, “among these sixteen people are five non-Polish nationals,” Kierwinski…
Authorities now say the gunman, who is a Polish citizen, is 25 years old.
The Portuguese Foreign Ministry said in a statement that a Portuguese woman was among the injured and was in hospital.

posts.title: Gunman was 'influenced by far-right ideology'
posts.text: A gunman who killed four women and two men in Krakow on Saturday was fascinated by far-right ideology, the interior minister Marcin Kierwinski told a news briefing. “Everything points to the fact that the shooter was influenced by far-right ideology, a matter that will also be subject to investigation,” Kierwinski…
Police spokesperson Andrzej Fijolek told broadcaster TVN 24 the assailant used an AR-15 rifle and that he had a firearms licence.

Poland’s defence minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz has rejected reports that the gunman was a “soldier in the Polish Armed Forces”. He said: “The man was not and is not a soldier in the Polish Armed Forces and has never had anything to do with the military.”

posts.title: Closing summary
posts.text: Thanks for following the blog tonight. The election has ended without a clear winner. Here are the top news lines from what will go down as one of New Zealand’s closest elections in many decades. Christopher Luxon’s National party and its right-leaning coalition partners are on the brink of a wafer-thin majority that…

Over the coming days and weeks we will get a sense of the magnitude of Qiulae Wong and the Opportunity party’s success tonight. Opportunity are currently projected to claim seven seats in parliament. Wong has said that if she held the tiebreaker power, she was open to negotiating with either a conservative or a…
A couple of pics of Christopher Luxon as he arrived to speak to supporters tonight.
On the current count, the Greens are celebrating a best-ever result of what looks to be 16 seats in parliament.

With 0.56% support, Te Pāti Māori will be stoked with its result tonight, writes Jamie Tahana. It seems odd, but the Māori party has spent the election deliberately asking people not to give them their party vote. Instead, they asked for electorate votes only. Just a reminder, seven of the seats in New Zealand’s…

So, hundreds of thousands of special votes are going to potentially change where things stand right now. In his speech tonight, Luxon said 300,000 special votes were yet to be counted. Those votes, which will be counted and known by 27 November, typically sway left. In the 2023 election there 600,000 special votes,…

posts.title: Right-bloc just ahead with 97% of vote counted
posts.text: In a 130-seat parliament, in which 66 seats are needed to govern, this is where things stand with 97% of the vote counted. However, special votes are still to be counted and the lay of the land will not be clear until 27 November. National 42, Act 13, NZ First 12 = 67 Labour 35, Greens 16, Te Pāti Māori 5 = 56…
Numbers… with 97% of the vote counted: National 29.3%, Labour 29.2%, Greens 13.3%, Act 11%, NZ First 9.8%, Opportunity 6%, Te Pāti Māori 0.6%.

Jamie Tahana has this hot-take on the Luxon speech: It was a tough line to tread for a speech: National is the biggest party on current results – 29.30% – but Luxon has also led the party to one of its most unpopular points, only 0.1% ahead of Labour. Luxon has also lost some of his most senior and experienced MPs,…

posts.title: Government 'caretaker conventions' will apply
posts.text: Luxon said that because of the closeness of the result, and with special votes still to be counted, caretaker conventions will apply. “For now, I want to tell New Zealanders that well established caretaker conventions apply … The daily business of government will continue.” Caretaker convention basically means that…

Jamie Tahana notes that for Luxon to continue as prime minister, he will have to cobble together a three- or four-party coalition, from a weakened position compared to 2023. In his speech, Luxon said: “Negotiations and compromises are going to be required … A number of races are still too close to call.”

Jamie Tahana has some more from the Luxon speech: Luxon called the election “too close to call”, and said “meaningful negotiations” for a new coalition government will start after the final results are known on 27 November. “It looks like an MMP special,” he said. “It’s heartening to see that so far National is once…
Luxon concedes result unlikely tonight, saying that meaningful negotiations will begin after final results on 27 November.
